sources.title: Helping Young Kids Cope with Social Anxiety
sources.publisher: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago (blog, 30 Oct 2025, expert source Dr. Miller Shivers)
sources.quote: Talk about what will happen. ... Let's make a plan together so this party feels easier. ... The goal isn't to push your child into being outgoing. ... you'll stay nearby so he can always find you.
sources.supports: For young children who find parties hard: talk about what will happen, plan together, do not push the child to be outgoing, and stay nearby so the child can find you. A hospital blog about social anxiety in young kids, used as general advice for a child who feels shy at a celebration; it does not say every child feels this way.

sources.title: Birthday parties for introverts
sources.quote: Planning with your child is crucial to pulling off a happy birthday. ... Or dispense with the ceremonial singing altogether and just hand out precut slices of cake or cupcakes. ... An easy solution is simply to have the child open the gifts later, after the guests have gone home. ... make a dramatic entrance carrying the cake into the room as the guests sing.
sources.supports: Plan the celebration with the child, the singing can be skipped, gifts can be opened later at home, and the child can carry the cake in. A parenting magazine article for children who hate having all eyes on them; applied to a gan birthday as general advice.

sources.title: How to Help Your Child Develop Empathy
sources.quote: Empathize with your child. ... Talk about others' feelings. ... Suggest how children can show empathy. ... Read stories about feelings.
sources.supports: Talk about how others feel, suggest to the child how to show empathy (for example offering a friend a favorite toy), and read stories about feelings. The page is about infants and toddlers; used as general support for the same ideas with a gan age child.

sources.title: Helping Young Kids Cope with Social Anxiety
sources.publisher: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago (blog, 30 Oct 2025, expert source Dr. Miller Shivers)
sources.quote: Talk about what will happen. ... Let's make a plan together so this party feels easier. ... The goal isn't to push your child into being outgoing. ... you'll stay nearby so he can always find you.
sources.supports: For young children who find parties hard: talk about what will happen, plan together, do not push the child to be outgoing, and stay nearby so the child can find you. A hospital blog about social anxiety in young kids, used as general advice for a child who feels shy at a celebration; it does not say every child feels this way.

sources.title: Birthday parties for introverts
sources.quote: Planning with your child is crucial to pulling off a happy birthday. ... Or dispense with the ceremonial singing altogether and just hand out precut slices of cake or cupcakes. ... An easy solution is simply to have the child open the gifts later, after the guests have gone home. ... make a dramatic entrance carrying the cake into the room as the guests sing.
sources.supports: Plan the celebration with the child, the singing can be skipped, gifts can be opened later at home, and the child can carry the cake in. A parenting magazine article for children who hate having all eyes on them; applied to a gan birthday as general advice.

sources.title: How to Help Your Child Develop Empathy
sources.quote: Empathize with your child. ... Talk about others' feelings. ... Suggest how children can show empathy. ... Read stories about feelings.
sources.supports: Talk about how others feel, suggest to the child how to show empathy (for example offering a friend a favorite toy), and read stories about feelings. The page is about infants and toddlers; used as general support for the same ideas with a gan age child.

sources.quote: Planning with your child is crucial to pulling off a happy birthday. ... Or dispense with the ceremonial singing altogether and just hand out precut slices of cake or cupcakes. ... sources.quote: Do something nice for their teacher – paint them a picture, bring them a treat or a coffee. ... Donate toys that they don't play with anymore. ... רק לא יודעת מה **עושים** איתן.
## מה יעזור לי:

slides.label: את חושבת:
slides.headline: ״היא לא רוצה לשתף״
slides.body:
את הבובה הכי אהובה שלי, נכון.

## אני עונה:
אני כן רוצה לתת משהו.
אולי צעצוע אחד שאני בוחרת **לבד**,
ושאת מראה לי איך מושיטים אותו.

משימה בגודל שלי.

שתסבירי לי למה אומרים תודה,
ולא רק תזכירי לי להגיד.

sources.title: 10 Ways to Teach Kindness to Preschoolers
sources.quote: Do something nice for their teacher – paint them a picture, bring them a treat or a coffee. ... Donate toys that they don't play with anymore. ... Smile at five people they see on the street. ... Invite all friends to play – excluding kids isn't nice. ... Let a sibling pick the movie they're going to watch. ... Draw a picture for a relative and send it to him or her in the mail. ... Help mom and dad with age-appropriate chores. ... Teach the "why" behind saying please and thank you. ... If you see someone being or doing something nice, point it out to your child. ... Share a favorite toy with a friend.
sources.supports: A list of small kindness acts for preschoolers: a picture for the teacher, donating toys, smiling at people, inviting everyone to play, letting a sibling choose the movie, a drawing for a relative, age-appropriate chores, the why behind please and thank you, pointing out kindness, sharing a favorite toy. A childcare company blog, used as general ideas.
